questions.scenario: A software engineer builds an autonomous customer support agent with the Claude Messages API. During integration testing, the agent terminates prematurely after its first tool invocation, returning raw JSON instead of completing the user request. Inspection reveals the application loop terminates as soon as `response.content[0].type == 'text'`. What is the correct loop termination condition?
options: Evaluate the response stop_reason field and terminate the loop only when it equals end_turn.
Inspect the message payload and terminate when the top-level role string transitions to user.
Check whether tool_use blocks exist in content and break immediately when any text block occurs.
Count consecutive iterations and terminate unconditionally when the cycle count reaches three.

rationales.correct: In the Messages API and Agent SDK, the model may return explanatory text alongside tool use blocks in the same turn. The loop must inspect response.stop_reason; it must continue executing tools when stop_reason is 'tool_use' and only present final results when stop_reason is 'end_turn'.
distractors: Checking whether role equals user is invalid because the assistant response always has the role 'assistant'.
Terminating when any text block occurs causes premature termination because Claude frequently emits thinking or commentary text prior to emitting a tool_use block.
Arbitrary cycle counting is an anti-pattern that truncates valid multi-step workflows before completion.

questions.keyInsight: Never terminate agentic loops by checking content text blocks or string parsing. Always inspect stop_reason: continue on 'tool_use' and terminate on 'end_turn'.

questions.scenario: A development team implements a multi-agent research platform using a hub-and-spoke topology with a primary coordinator delegating to web search, document analysis, and synthesis subagents. Peer-to-peer communication bypasses coordinator state tracking, creating unmonitored execution loops.
The Claude Messages API rejects requests containing messages generated by unauthorized child models.
Direct communication between subagents incurs double token billing across shared network interfaces.

The Messages API is stateless and does not track or reject requests based on which child subagent generated prior content.
